I fixed this in `UberJarBuilder.java`, but I couldn't compile or test it. Both Maven attempts failed on environment problems (Develocity extension offline, then unresolved parent POM versions). I added no tests, per the rules.

**Cause:** `walkFileDependencyForDependency` opened each dependency's path tree and closed it as soon as the walk finished. The parallel archive creator only reads the dependency files later, when `close()` writes the zip. The old comment said the shared tree stays open until the Quarkus classloaders close. That doesn't hold in a multi-threaded Maven build. Another module's build can close the shared (cached) zip filesystem for the same dependency jar first. The read then fails with `ClosedFileSystemException`. The issue reports the same failure surfacing as "Unable to create archive".

**Fix:** In `buildUberJar0`, the open trees are collected in a list. A `Closeable` declared before the archive creator in the try-with-resources closes them. That means they're closed only after the archive has been fully written. `walkFileDependencyForDependency` now takes that list, adds each tree to it, and no longer closes the tree itself. I also removed the comment that gave the wrong reason it was safe to close.

I didn't check `AbstractFastJarBuilder`, which opens trees at line 479 and may need a similar change.

I also didn't build the call graph or log any findings for the axiomengine dogfooding. I read the code directly, so the graph isn't evaluated for this task.
